relevance_note: Case series of four children with HA20: "We describe four unrelated patients evaluated at a single tertiary center, each carrying a distinct TNFAIP3 mutation".
method_note: Read the paper in full and entered every value by hand into a Python builder script (scratch dir); no table was transcribed by script. Table 1 has patients as rows; spans quote from the patient label through the cell. Labels: probands use the paper's 'Patient A'-'Patient D'. The paper gives no unique labels for relatives or for previously published patients, so labels were constructed from the relation and the proband (only 'father of patient B' is verbatim); family_label uses the paper's case numbers. is_proband = true for A-D as the four index patients of the series (the paper does not use the word proband). Omitted people: relatives described only as unaffected and not tested (A's brother, B's mother, B's second brother, C's two sisters), and the mother and grandmother (diagnosed with Behcet's) of the previously reported p.Q379* patient. D's parents are included because they were tested (negative). Four previously published patients summarised in the Discussion are their own rows with source_reference_in_review. Possible duplicate: the p.Trp168* patient 'with both HA20 and DLBCL' is cited with '(24)' in the clause 'as found in the father of patient B (24)'; the paper does not say whether this is the same person as B's father, so the two were not merged and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is left null. variant_type 'nonsense' for B, C and D is deduced from 'Three out of four patients had non-sense mutations' plus A being the only missense; no per-patient statement. B's inheritance recorded as paternal because her father 'has HA20 of the same genetic variant'; the mother is called unaffected but her testing is not stated. Pathogenicity for p.Trp168* and p.Q379* is the authors' citation of ClinVar RCV accessions (RCV005102078.1, RCV005052457.1), and for p.Arg271* refs 17-21 (Infevers etc.): this is database-derived wording printed in the paper, which may matter for concordance scoring. Lab values recorded as observed without the word 'positive'/'elevated': A's ANA 1:160 and 1:80; D's CRP 60.9 mg/L. Checklist judgments: poor weight gain -> growth failure (observed); DLBCL -> lymphoproliferation (observed) for B's father and the p.Trp168* literature patient; epilepsy -> CNS involvement (observed) for D's brother, but neurodevelopmental delay (A's sister) left not reported; B's father's 'aphthous ulcers' not mapped to oral ulcers because the paper also uses 'bipolar aphthous ulcers'; A's negative screening for uveitis and retinal vasculitis is narrower than 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' and 'vasculitis', so both stay not reported; B's fever 'with pericarditis' not counted as recurrent fever; C's infant watery/bloody stools and B's mildly raised calprotectin and duodenal lymphoid aggregates not counted as GI inflammation; D's normal pulmonary CT not counted as excluding interstitial lung disease. D's age at HA20 diagnosis is not stated (testing followed the presentation at 13 years), so left not reported. First author: header 'Jayaraman Sahana' with contributions 'SJ' read as surname Jayaraman. No group statement names patients, so no 'inferred from group statement' rows. Contradictions found: none at patient level (Table 1 and the case texts agree on onset, sex and main features).
